claim: Curaxin CBL0137 destabilizes nucleosomes via disruption of histone/DNA interactions.
source: We previously found that DNA demethylation on p53-deficient background leads to transcription of repetitive heterochromatin elements, followed by an interferon response, a phenomenon we named TRAIN (Transcription of Repeats Activates INterferon). Here, we report that curaxin, an anticancer small molecule, destabilizing nucleosomes via disruption of histone/DNA interactions, also induces TRAIN.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a direct assertion about the mechanism of curaxin action.

claim: Curaxin inhibits oncogene-induced transformation in an interferon-dependent manner.
source: Furthermore, curaxin inhibits oncogene-induced transformation and tumor growth in mice in an interferon-dependent manner, suggesting that anticancer activity of curaxin, previously attributed to p53-activation and NF-kappaB-inhibition, may also involve induction of interferon response to epigenetic derepression of the cellular 'repeatome'.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing transformation assays with Ifnar1 knockout cells.

claim: Curaxin inhibits tumor growth in mice in an interferon-dependent manner.
source: Furthermore, curaxin inhibits oncogene-induced transformation and tumor growth in mice in an interferon-dependent manner, suggesting that anticancer activity of curaxin, previously attributed to p53-activation and NF-kappaB-inhibition, may also involve induction of interferon response to epigenetic derepression of the cellular 'repeatome'.
evidence: This is supported by tumor growth experiments in Ifnar1-/- mice shown in Figure 9.

claim: HDAC inhibitors also induce TRAIN.
source: Moreover, we observed that another type of drugs decondensing chromatin, HDAC inhibitor, also induces TRAIN.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing TSA (an HDAC inhibitor) induces interferon response in MEF cells.

claim: TRAIN may be a mechanism ensuring epigenetic integrity of mammalian cells via elimination of cells with desilenced chromatin.
source: Thus, we proposed that TRAIN may be one of the mechanisms ensuring epigenetic integrity of mammalian cells via elimination of cells with desilenced chromatin.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the observed phenomena.

claim: Curaxins bind DNA via intercalation of the carbazole body accompanied by protrusion of side chains into DNA grooves.
source: Our search for the mechanism of action of curaxins resulted in the discovery that curaxins bind DNA via intercalation of the carbazole body accompanied by the protrusion of two side chains into the major groove and a third side chain into the minor groove of DNA.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017) and represents established data.

claim: Curaxins have no effect on DNA chemical structure and do not cause DNA damage in mammalian cells.
source: Curaxins have no effect on DNA chemical structure, that is, they do not cause any DNA damage in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is stated as a direct observation from previous studies.

claim: Curaxin binding to DNA changes both the helical shape and flexibility of DNA and reduces its negative charge.
source: However, their binding to DNA changes both the helical shape and flexibility of DNA and reduces its negative charge (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Alterations of DNA helical shape, charge and flexibility caused by curaxins force DNA to dissociate from the histone octamer in vitro and in vivo.
source: Alterations of DNA helical shape, charge and flexibility, caused by curaxins, force DNA to dissociate from the octamer in vitro and in vivo (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: At lower concentrations of CBL0137, DNA is unfolded from H2A/H2B dimers leading to their detachment.
source: At lower concentrations of curaxin CBL0137, DNA is first unfolded from the outer parts of the nucleosome, that is, from H2A/H2B dimers located at both sides of the inner H3/H4 tetramer, which leads to the detachment of the H2A/H2B dimer(s) and exposure of the surface of the H3/H4 tetramer.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: At higher CBL0137 concentrations, DNA is unwrapped from the H3/H4 tetramer leading to complete nucleosome disassembly.
source: At higher CBL0137 concentrations, DNA is unwrapped from the inner H3/H4 tetramer, which leads to complete nucleosome disassembly (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Treatment of cells with CBL0137 causes massive transition of B-DNA into left-handed Z-DNA form.
source: We have shown a massive transition of right-handed B-DNA in cells treated with curaxin CBL0137 into the left-handed Z-DNA form (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Treatment of cells with CBL0137 leads to dose-dependent destabilization and disassembly of chromatin in the absence of DNA damage.
source: Thus, treatment of cells with CBL0137 leads to dose-dependent destabilization and disassembly of chromatin in the absence of DNA damage and, most importantly, of the classical DNA damage response, providing an opportunity to study how a cell reacts to chromatin damage and the role of chromatin perturbations in the anticancer activity of curaxins.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from previous work and provides the rationale for the current study.

claim: No phosphorylation of p53 N-terminal serines was detected in curaxin-treated cells.
source: However, no phosphorylation of p53 N-terminal serines, which are obligatory markers of the DNA damage response, was detected in curaxin-treated cells.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Gasparian et al., 2011).

claim: There was no activation of DNA-damage-sensitive kinases (ATM, ATR, DNA-PK) in curaxin-treated cells.
source: Furthermore, there was no activation of DNA-damage-sensitive kinases, such as ATM, ATR, and DNA-PK.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Gasparian et al., 2011).

claim: p53 in curaxin-treated cells was phosphorylated at serine 392 by casein kinase 2 (CK2).
source: Instead, p53 in curaxin-treated cells was phosphorylated at serine 392 by casein kinase 2 (CK2) that formed a complex with the histone chaperone Facilitates Chromatin Transcription (FACT) (Gasparian et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Gasparian et al., 2011).

claim: FACT consists of two conservative proteins present in all eukaryotes, SPT16 and SSRP1.
source: FACT consists of two conservative proteins present in all eukaryotes, Suppressor of Ty 16 (SPT16) and Structure Specific Recognition Protein 1 (SSRP1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FACT composition.

claim: In basal conditions FACT is involved in transcription elongation.
source: In basal conditions FACT is involved in transcription elongation (Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003), (Gurova and Studitsky, 2018; in preparation).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Human FACT binds poorly intact nucleosomes.
source: Human FACT binds poorly intact nucleosomes (Tsunaka et al., 2016), (Safina et al., 2017)
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Nucleosome disassembly caused by curaxin opens multiple FACT-binding sites normally hidden inside the nucleosome.
source: We have found that nucleosome disassembly caused by curaxin opens multiple FACT-binding sites, which are normally hidden inside the nucleosome.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Chromatin unfolding occurs first in heterochromatic regions.
source: Chromatin unfolding occurs first in heterochromatic regions, and all cellular FACT is rapidly relocated into these regions and depleted from the nucleoplasm (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: All cellular FACT is rapidly relocated into heterochromatic regions and depleted from the nucleoplasm after curaxin treatment.
source: Chromatin unfolding occurs first in heterochromatic regions, and all cellular FACT is rapidly relocated into these regions and depleted from the nucleoplasm (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: FACT binds Z-DNA via the CID domain of the SSRP1 subunit.
source: We also observed that FACT not only binds partially disassembled nucleosomes but also Z-DNA via the CID (c-terminal intrinsically disordered) domain of the SSRP1 subunit (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: The HMG domain of SSRP1 binds non-B DNA, bent or cruciform.
source: Importantly, it was already known that the immediate neighboring domain, HMG (high mobility group), also binds non-B DNA, bent or cruciform (Gariglio et al., 1997; Krohn et al., 2003; Yarnell et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: SSRP1 binding to DNA results in CK2-mediated signal for p53 activation.
source: In all cases of SSRP1 binding to DNA, there is a CK2-mediated signal for p53 activation (Gasparian et al., 2011; Krohn et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: CBL0137 activates transcription from heterochromatic regions normally silenced in cells, including centromeric and pericentromeric repeats and endogenous retroviral elements.
source: We found that independently of the presence of FACT, CBL0137 activates transcription from heterochromatic regions normally silenced in cells, including centromeric and pericentromeric repeats and endogenous retroviral elements, associated with accumulation of double-stranded RNAs (dsRNA) in cells and activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing increased transcription of repetitive elements.

claim: CBL0137 treatment is associated with accumulation of double-stranded RNAs (dsRNA) in cells.
source: We found that independently of the presence of FACT, CBL0137 activates transcription from heterochromatic regions normally silenced in cells, including centromeric and pericentromeric repeats and endogenous retroviral elements, associated with accumulation of double-stranded RNAs (dsRNA) in cells and activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining with dsRNA antibody.

claim: CBL0137 treatment leads to activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response.
source: We found that independently of the presence of FACT, CBL0137 activates transcription from heterochromatic regions normally silenced in cells, including centromeric and pericentromeric repeats and endogenous retroviral elements, associated with accumulation of double-stranded RNAs (dsRNA) in cells and activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response.
evidence: This is supported by multiple assays including RT-PCR, Western blot, and reporter assays.

claim: TRAIN was observed previously upon DNA demethylation.
source: This phenomenon, named TRAIN (Transcription of Repeats Activates INterferon) (Leonova et al., 2013) was observed previously upon DNA demethylation (Chiappinelli et al., 2015; Guryanova et al., 2016; Roulois et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Liver and lung were selected as FACT-negative tissues.
source: Liver and lung were selected as FACT-negative, and spleen and testis were used as FACT-positive tissues ([Garcia et al., 2011] and Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 1A and cited from previous work.

claim: Spleen and testis were used as FACT-positive tissues.
source: Liver and lung were selected as FACT-negative, and spleen and testis were used as FACT-positive tissues ([Garcia et al., 2011] and Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by IHC staining shown in Figure 1A and cited from previous work.

claim: Expression of Ifit3 gene was upregulated in all organs >1.5-fold with p<0.05 in response to CBL0137.
source: There was almost no overlap in genes downregulated in response to CBL0137 among different organs (Figure 1B, Figure 2—source data 1–6). However, expression of one gene, Ifit3, was upregulated in all organs > 1.5-fold with p<0.05 (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The interferon (IFN) signaling pathway was upregulated in response to doses above 30 mg/kg CBL0137 in all organs except testis.
source: The interferon (IFN) signaling pathway was upregulated in response to doses above 30 mg/kg in all organs except testis, which was not analyzed due to the low number of upregulated genes (Figure 2A, Figure 2 – Figure Supplement 1 and Figure 2—source data 1–6).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The transcription factors that regulate genes elevated in response to CBL0137 are STAT1, IRF1, IRF8 and IRF7.
source: The transcription factors that regulate genes elevated in response to CBL0137 are STAT1, IRF1, IRF8 and IRF7 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: CBL0137 treatment leads to activation of the IFN response in all tissues independently of FACT expression.
source: This analysis suggested that CBL0137 treatment leads to the activation of the IFN response in all tissues independently of FACT expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that IFN response is activated in both FACT-positive and FACT-negative tissues.

claim: CBL0137 inhibits NF-kappaB via a FACT-dependent mechanism.
source: We have shown previously that CBL0137 inhibits NF-kappaB via a FACT-dependent mechanism (Gasparian et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: The peak of Irf7 mRNA induction was seen at 24 hr following treatment with either 60 or 90 mg/kg CBL0137.
source: The peak of induction was already seen at 24 hr following treatment with either 60 or 90 mg/kg CBL0137, while 30 mg/kg showed slower kinetics (Figure 3D,E, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Increased levels of Isg15 and Usp18 transcripts were detected as early as 6 hrs post-treatment with 90 mg/kg CBL0137 and reached a peak at 12 hr.
source: Increased levels of two other IFN responsive transcripts, Isg15 and Usp18, were detected as early as 6 hrspost-treatment with 90 mg/kg CBL0137 and reached a peak at 12 hr, then gradually declined (Figure 3F,G, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: The CBL0137-induced IFN response is faster than that reported with other small molecules and is closer to the response observed with biologicals.
source: Thus, the CBL0137-induced IFN response is faster than that reported with other small molecules and is closer to the response observed with biologicals.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of kinetics data with literature reports.

claim: CBL0137 causes a rapid and robust induction of the IFN response in all tissues of mice that were tested.
source: Experiments with mice demonstrated that CBL0137 caused a rapid and robust induction of the IFN response in all tissues of mice that were tested.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experiments showing IFN response in different mouse tissues.

claim: CBL0137 induces an increase in mRNA and protein levels of IFN-inducible genes in both human and mouse fibroblasts.
source: We detected an increase in mRNA and protein levels of IFN-inducible genes in both human and mouse fibroblasts (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Effect of CBL0137 on IFN-inducible genes was stronger on p53 null than in p53 wild-type MEF.
source: Effect was stronger on p53 null, than in p53 wild-type MEF (Figure 4B,C), as we observed before with DNA demethylating agents (Leonova et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 4B,C and cited from previous work.

claim: No induction of IFN-inducible genes was detected in tumor cells of mouse or human origin.
source: However, no induction of IFN-inducible genes was detected in tumor cells of mouse or human origin.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: Different components of the IFN response are frequently inactivated in tumors.
source: Since different components of the IFN response are frequently inactivated in tumors (Kulaeva et al., 2003), we employed a reporter assay that detected an IFN response through the activation of a consensus IFN-sensitive response element (ISRE), which drove the expression of mCherry or luciferase (Imam et al., 1990).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: CBL0137 induces an IFN response in both mouse and human tumor cells as detected by ISRE reporter assay.
source: Using these assays, we observed that CBL0137 also induces an IFN response in both mouse and human tumor cells (Figure 4D,E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: A deficiency in Ifnar1 reduced the induction of Ifit3 expression after CBL0137.
source: A deficiency in either Ifnar1 and Irf7 reduced or eliminated the induction of Ifit3 expression after CBL0137, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A deficiency in Irf7 eliminated the induction of Ifit3 expression after CBL0137.
source: A deficiency in either Ifnar1 and Irf7 reduced or eliminated the induction of Ifit3 expression after CBL0137, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The loss of p53 stimulated the IFN response to CBL0137.
source: In contrast, the loss of p53 stimulated the response.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: There was no effect of Irf1 knockout on the induction of Ifit3 expression after CBL0137.
source: There was no effect of Irf1 knockout (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: High doses of CBL0137 caused disassembly of nucleosomes in cells, which led to extensive negative supercoiling of DNA and a transition from B-DNA into left-handed Z-DNA.
source: Importantly, we have recently shown that high doses of CBL0137 caused disassembly of nucleosomes in cells, which led to the extensive negative supercoiling of DNA and a transition from B-DNA into left-handed Z-DNA (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: The loss of ZBP1 expression did not significantly change the induction of ISRE-mCherry reporter activity by CBL0137.
source: We compared the effect of CBL0137 on ISRE-mCherry reporter activity in these cells to wild-type cells and cells transduced with control gRNA and observed insignificant changes in the induction of the reporter activity 48 hr after CBL0137 treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There was no Z-DNA present in the cells treated with CBL0137 doses that caused a robust IFN response.
source: Importantly, there was no Z-DNA present in the cells treated with CBL0137 doses that caused a robust IFN response as judged by the absence of staining with Z-DNA antibodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Z-DNA transition induced by CBL0137 does not play role in the induction of IFN response in CBL0137-treated cells.
source: Thus, we concluded that Z-DNA transition induced by CBL0137 does not play role in the induction of IFN response in CBL0137-treated cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the ZBP1 knockout and Z-DNA staining experiments.

claim: Increased staining with dsRNA antibody was observed in CBL0137-treated cells.
source: Using an antibody to dsRNA (Targett-Adams et al., 2008), we observed increased staining in CBL0137-treated cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: After CBL0137 treatment, a single lower molecular weight band appeared that was strongly bound by the B1 probe.
source: After CBL0137 treatment, a single lower molecular weight band appeared that was strongly bound by the B1 probe and was similar in size and abundance to the band in cells treated with the positive control (5-aza-cytidine (5-aza)) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: RNA-seq analysis demonstrated a significant increase in the number of transcripts corresponding to several classes of endogenous viruses as well as GSAT and SATMIN repeats in CBL0137-treated cells.
source: This analysis demonstrated a significant increase in the number of transcripts corresponding to several classes of endogenous viruses as well as GSAT (pericentromeric) and SATMIN (centromeric) repeats in cells (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Treatment with CBL0137 leads to the activation of the transcription of heterochromatic regions, which are not or minimally transcribed under basal conditions.
source: These data suggest that treatment with CBL0137 leads to the activation of the transcription of heterochromatic regions, which are not or minimally transcribed under basal conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA-seq data showing increased transcription of repetitive elements.

claim: Loss of FACT via c-trapping may lead to activation of silenced transcription since mutations of FACT subunits in yeast causes transcription from cryptic sites.
source: Loss of FACT via c-trapping may lead to activation of silenced transcription since mutations of FACT subunits in yeast causes transcription from cryptic sites that are covered by nucleosomes in basal conditions (Mason and Struhl, 2003), (Jamai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from previous work in yeast.

claim: FACT is important for chromatin assembly at centromeres.
source: FACT is also important for chromatin assembly at centromeres (Okada et al., 2009; Prendergast et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: CBL0137 treatment increased the proportion of GFP-expressing cells in HeLa-TI cells.
source: An increase in the proportion of GFP-expressing cells was also observed after CBL0137 treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Both TSA and CBL0137 induced expression of Ifit3 and Irf7 genes in MEF cells.
source: In MEF cells, both TSA and CBL0137 induced expression of Ifit3 and Irf7 genes (Figure 7B)
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: TSA caused only a weak increase in ISRE reporter activity (1.5 folds versus >5 folds for CBL0137) only at the highest concentration (500 nM).
source: TSA caused only a weak increase in ISRE reporter activity (1.5 folds versus >5 folds for CBL0137) only at the highest concentration (500 nM, Figure 7C) when evidence of toxicity was present.
evidence: This is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: TSA treatment caused an increase in acetylated histone H3 levels.
source: As expected, TSA treatment caused an increase in acetylated histone H3 levels, while CBL0137 decreased the amount of chromatin-bound histone H3 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: CBL0137 decreased the amount of chromatin-bound histone H3.
source: As expected, TSA treatment caused an increase in acetylated histone H3 levels, while CBL0137 decreased the amount of chromatin-bound histone H3 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Substantial loss of core histones (chromatin disassembly) was observed with approximately 5 μM CBL0137.
source: However, as we saw previously (Safina et al., 2017), substantial loss of core histones (i.e. chromatin disassembly) was observed with approximately 5 μM CBL0137, which is much higher than the concentrations at which we observed TRAIN (0.5–1 μM).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Nucleosome 'opening' may be enough to create conditions for TRAIN without nucleosome disassembly or dissociation of nucleosome parts.
source: We proposed that nucleosome 'opening,' that is, the state of loose contact between the DNA and histone core without loss of histones from the core (proposed in the review [Zlatanova et al., 2009]), may be enough to create conditions for TRAIN. Namely, no nucleosome disassembly or dissociation of nucleosome parts is needed.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the observation that TRAIN occurs at lower CBL0137 concentrations than those causing nucleosome disassembly.

claim: CBL0137 treatment led to a redistribution of H1.5 from the chromatin to the nucleoli.
source: CBL0137 treatment led to a redistribution of H1.5 from the chromatin to the nucleoli, similarly to the effect of CBL0137 on core histones (Safina et al., 2017) but this phenomenon was observed at a faster and at much lower CBL0137 concentrations (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: TRAIN in CBL0137-treated cells was observed at the same concentration range as redistribution of histone H1 and before the disassembly of the nucleosome core.
source: TRAIN in CBL0137-treated cells was observed at the same concentration range as redistribution of histone H1 and before the disassembly of the nucleosome core, suggesting that nucleosome opening is sufficient to allow the transcription of heterochromatic regions in cells.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the concentration ranges for different effects.

claim: Nucleosome opening is sufficient to allow the transcription of heterochromatic regions in cells.
source: TRAIN in CBL0137-treated cells was observed at the same concentration range as redistribution of histone H1 and before the disassembly of the nucleosome core, suggesting that nucleosome opening is sufficient to allow the transcription of heterochromatic regions in cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that TRAIN occurs before nucleosome disassembly.

claim: The degree of TRAIN depends on cell type and the mode of chromatin opening.
source: Thus, we observed the presence of TRAIN using different chromatin modifying agents; however, its degree depends on cell type and the mode of chromatin opening.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the effects of CBL0137 and TSA in different cell types.

claim: Administration of CBL0137 to tumor prone mice prior to tumor onset significantly reduced the incidence of cancer and diminished the occurrence of aggressive forms of breast cancer.
source: We have previously shown that administration of CBL0137 to tumor prone mice prior to tumor onset significantly reduced the incidence of cancer and diminished the occurrence of aggressive forms of breast cancer (Koman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Activation of IFN may be an additional mechanism to eliminate transformed cells, because they are more sensitive to IFN-mediated apoptosis than normal cells.
source: However, activation of IFN may be an additional mechanism to eliminate transformed cells, because they are more sensitive to IFN-mediated apoptosis than normal cells (reviewed in [Parker et al., 2016]).
evidence: This is cited from a review.

claim: The number of transformed foci was significantly reduced in cells treated with CBL0137 compared to untreated cells, but only if the cells had functional IFN receptor (Ifnar1+/+).
source: After 10 days, the number of transformed foci was significantly reduced in cells treated with CBL0137 compared to untreated cells, but only if the cells had functional IFN receptor (Ifnar1+/+, Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by transformation assay data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: TRAIN may be an additional mechanism by which CBL0137 exerts its tumor preventive effect.
source: Thus, TRAIN may be an additional mechanism by which CBL0137 exerts its tumor preventive effect.
evidence: This is inferred from the transformation assay results.

claim: Wild type tumors did not grow at all since the start of CBL0137 treatment, while Ifanr1-/- tumors continued growing, albeit slower than vehicle treated tumors.
source: Wild type tumors did not grow at all since the start of treatment, while Ifanr1-/- tumors continued growing, albeit slower than vehicle treated tumors (Figure 9B,C).
evidence: This is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 9B,C.

claim: Induction of IFN response by CBL0137 is an important component of the anticancer activity of CBL0137.
source: Thus, induction of IFN response by CBL0137 is an important component of the anticancer activity of CBL0137.
evidence: This is inferred from the tumor growth experiments in Ifnar1-/- mice.

claim: At lower concentrations of CBL0137 (<1 μM in cells), the nucleosome 'opens,' loses the linker histone H1 without dissociation or loss of core histones.
source: At lower concentrations of CBL0137 (<1 μM in cells), the nucleosome 'opens,' loses the linker histone H1 without dissociation or loss of core histones.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data showing H1 redistribution.

claim: At higher CBL0137 concentrations (1–5 μM), dimer detachment occurs with occasional loss of core histones.
source: At higher CBL0137 concentrations (1–5 μM), dimer detachment occurs with occasional loss of core histones.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: At CBL0137 concentrations greater than 5 μM, the nucleosome is disassembled, and core histones are evicted from the chromatin.
source: At CBL0137 concentrations greater than 5 μM, the nucleosome is disassembled, and core histones are evicted from the chromatin.
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: After a short incubation with <1 μM CBL0137, the drug can be washed from the cells with almost no harm to the cells.
source: Indeed, after a short incubation with <1 μM CBL0137, the drug can be washed from the cells with almost no harm to the cells
evidence: This is stated as an observation about reversibility of CBL0137 effects.

claim: Cells incubated with 1–3 μM CBL0137 for no more than 1 hr survive with some loss of viability.
source: cells incubated with 1–3 μM CBL0137 for no more than 1 hr survive with some loss of viability.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about reversibility of CBL0137 effects.

claim: Treatment with >5 μM CBL0137 for more than 15 min leads to complete cell death after 48 hr.
source: However, treatment with >5 μM CBL0137 for more than 15 min leads to complete cell death after 48 hr, which is in line with the complete disassembly of chromatin (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation about irreversibility of CBL0137 effects at high concentrations.

claim: The first cellular factor that 'reacts' to the problems with chromatin packaging in CBL0137-treated cells was histone chaperone FACT, which underwent c-trapping in response to nucleosome disassembly.
source: The first cellular factor that we found, 'reacting' to the problems with chromatin packaging in CBL0137-treated cells, was histone chaperone FACT, which underwent c-trapping in response to nucleosome disassembly (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: Human FACT cannot bind and uncoil a 'closed' nucleosome.
source: It was shown that human FACT cannot bind and uncoil a 'closed' nucleosome (Tsunaka et al., 2016; Valieva et al., 2017) (Figure 10).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Nucleosome opening allows FACT to invade the nucleosome and bind the H3/H4 tetramer via the middle domain of SPT16 and the H2A/H2B dimer via the c-terminal portions of both subunits.
source: However, nucleosome opening most probably allows FACT to invade the nucleosome and bind the H3/H4 tetramer via the middle domain of SPT16 and the H2A/H2B dimer via the c-terminal portions of both subunits (Belotserkovskaya et al., 2003; Kemble et al., 2015; Tsunaka et al., 2016; Winkler and Luger, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: SPT16-mediated 'n (nucleosome)-trapping' is observed at 0.3–1 μM CBL0137.
source: In cells, we see this as SPT16-mediated 'n (nucleosome)-trapping,' which is observed at 0.3–1 μM CBL0137.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the current study.

claim: At CBL0137 concentrations greater than 3 μM, significant negative supercoiling caused base-unpairing of DNA and the transition of B-DNA into left-handed Z-form DNA, which is bound by FACT via the c-terminal intrinsically disordered domain of SSRP1 subunit.
source: At CBL0137 concentrations greater than 3 μM, significant negative supercoiling, as a result of nucleosome disassembly, caused base-unpairing of DNA and the transition of B-DNA into left-handed Z-form DNA, which is bound by FACT via the c-terminal intrinsically disordered domain of SSRP1 subunit (Safina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work (Safina et al., 2017).

claim: The most prominent and uniform change observed in the presence and absence of FACT was activation of the IFN response in all tested organs and cells at both the mRNA and protein levels.
source: The most prominent and uniform change observed in the presence and absence of FACT was activation of the IFN response in all tested organs and cells at both the mRNA and protein levels.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The induction of IFN-sensitive genes (ISG) has a bell-shaped curve, with a maximum increase at a CBL0137 concentration of approximately 0.5–1 μM.
source: The induction of IFN-sensitive genes (ISG) has a bell-shaped curve, with a maximum increase at a CBL0137 concentration of approximately 0.5–1 μM, which corresponds to nucleosome 'opening' followed by the inhibition of transcription at concentrations greater than 1 μM, when nucleosome disassembly starts.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: IFN is activated in response to the dsRNA formed due to the increased transcription from normally silenced constitutive heterochromatin.
source: We believe that IFN is activated in response to the dsRNA formed due to the increased transcription from normally silenced constitutive heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental observations.

claim: Displacement of histone H1 may make heterochromatin accessible for RNA polymerase, while accessibility of genomic regions not locked with H1 does not change.
source: We propose that displacement of histone H1 may make heterochromatin accessible for RNA polymerase, while accessibility of genomic regions not locked with H1 does not change.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism to explain selective transcription of heterochromatin.

claim: The anticancer effect in mice is seen at concentrations that activate the IFN response.
source: Importantly, the anticancer effect in mice is seen at concentrations that activate the IFN response, suggesting that chromatin opening without chromatin disassembly is enough to cause an anticancer effect in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the effective concentrations for different effects.

claim: Chromatin opening without chromatin disassembly is enough to cause an anticancer effect in vivo.
source: Importantly, the anticancer effect in mice is seen at concentrations that activate the IFN response, suggesting that chromatin opening without chromatin disassembly is enough to cause an anticancer effect in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that anticancer effects occur at lower concentrations than those causing nucleosome disassembly.

claim: Activation of the IFN response by CBL0137 creates an opportunity to use IFN-responsive factors as pharmacodynamic markers of curaxin activity in the clinic.
source: Activation of the IFN response by CBL0137 also creates an opportunity to use IFN-responsive factors as pharmacodynamic markers of curaxin activity in the clinic, since many of these factors are secreted and were detected in the plasma of mice.
evidence: This is a proposed application based on the experimental findings.

claim: Curaxins may be used as a tool to affect chromatin organization and folding globally in cells and animals to study the consequences of an abrupt loss of epigenetic regulation in vivo.
source: Thus, curaxins, compounds with established anticancer activity in multiple preclinical models, may also be used as a tool to affect chromatin organization and folding globally in cells and animals to study the consequences of an abrupt loss of epigenetic regulation in vivo.
evidence: This is a proposed application of curaxins based on their mechanism of action.

claim: The property of curaxins to affect chromatin organization may be useful for reprogramming and other types of therapeutic epigenetic manipulations.
source: Potentially, this property of curaxins may be useful for reprogramming and other types of therapeutic epigenetic manipulations.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about potential applications.

claim: TRAIN may be a more general response to the problems associated with chromatin packaging and the danger of the loss of epigenetic integrity.
source: Based on this data, we propose that TRAIN may be a more general response to the problems associated with chromatin packaging and the danger of the loss of epigenetic integrity.
evidence: This is a proposed generalization based on observing TRAIN in multiple contexts.

claim: TRAIN may be a mechanism triggered by elevated expression of silenced repetitive genomic elements and executed by the IFN response, which is capable of killing cells.
source: It is tempting to speculate that TRAIN may be such a mechanism, triggered by elevated expression of silenced repetitive genomic elements and executed by the IFN response, which is capable of killing cells.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the function of TRAIN.

claim: TRAIN mechanism may have evolved in response to real viral threats, especially in the form of the expansion of endogenous retroviral elements.
source: It is likely that this mechanism evolved in response to real viral threats, especially in the form of the expansion of endogenous retroviral elements.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the evolutionary origin of TRAIN.

claim: TRAIN mechanism may serve as an epigenetic lock, which supports the differentiation state and limits cell plasticity.
source: This mechanism may serve as an epigenetic lock, which supports the differentiation state and limits cell plasticity and, therefore, the ability to transdifferentiate and regenerate organs and tissues, as well as to undergo epigenetic transitions associated with malignant transformation and tumor progression.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the function of TRAIN in maintaining cell identity.
